comparison: Both evaluate claims C49-C52 regarding flagellar reorientation and force balance during gliding. OpenEval finds the kymography observations and force balance model well-supported. Peer reviewers challenge the interpretation, noting that the caption to Figure 5 incorrectly emphasizes flagellum-lifting as the typical reversal mechanism when most reversals occur with both flagella remaining in contact with the substrate.

Both evaluate claims C71-C80, C91 regarding viscous drag measurements. OpenEval finds the convergence of multiple measurement methods convincing and the exclusion of motor backsteps well-reasoned. Peer reviewers raise significant methodological concerns about whether the measured drag truly reflects membrane viscosity alone, questioning the mode of failure (motor vs. glycoprotein detachment) and noting that dynein backsteps are hard to rule out.

Both evaluate calcium-dependence claims C53-C59, C94-C96. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree that the calcium manipulation experiments are well-executed and support the interpretation that Ca2+ regulates FMG1-B attachment rather than motor activity. No concerns raised about this mechanistic conclusion.

Both evaluate claims C81-C84, C103-C104 regarding reciprocal motor coordination. OpenEval and peer reviewers agree that temperature-sensitive mutant experiments provide strong evidence against tug-of-war and support reciprocal coordination. The findings are accepted without objection.

Both evaluate colocalization claims C22-C26, C85-C86. OpenEval finds the multicolor tracking and correlation analysis robust. Peer reviewers accept the colocalization findings, with comment 7 requesting only technical clarification about fluorescence variation rather than challenging the core result.

Both evaluate broader implications claims C7, C60, C105-C110, C112, C115 regarding IFT's role in signaling. OpenEval marks these as UNCERTAIN, noting they mix supported findings with extensive speculation requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers accept these as reasonable speculative suggestions presented appropriately as possibilities rather than definitive conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive dynein-1b and mutant analysis claims C4, C27-C47, C87-C88. Peer R3 evaluates subset C33-C45 (dynein-1b findings). Both find the evidence convincing. Peer comment 6 notes temperature independence as interesting observation but doesn't dispute results.

Both evaluate IFT pausing claims C27-C32. OpenEval finds the evidence from temperature-sensitive mutants and pharmacological inhibition convincing. Peer reviewers find the pausing 'abundantly clear and quite convincing in Video 2' but request better visualization in figures. Both accept the underlying finding.

Both evaluate force measurement claims C61-C63, C65. OpenEval finds optical trapping with simultaneous fluorescence imaging provides strong support for motor number estimates. Peer reviewers accept the force measurements and motor estimates without challenge (peer R5 also includes C100, C102 comparing to Laib et al.).

Both address claim C64 regarding whether peak forces represent a lower boundary. OpenEval finds the calculation straightforward and the 'at least four motors' conclusion conservative and well-justified. Peer reviewers explicitly state this claim is 'not well supported by the data,' directly challenging the interpretation about motors not reaching maximum stall force.

Both evaluate contextualization claims C100, C102 comparing current findings to Laib et al. OpenEval finds the methodological advance and critical assessment of prior work appropriate. Peer reviewers accept the comparison without challenge.

Both evaluate mechanistic model claims C4, C46-C47, C87-C88 (with peer R10 also including C3, C89). OpenEval finds multiple converging lines of evidence support the model. Peer reviewers accept the overall mechanism of how paused IFT trains drive gliding motility through dynein-1b force generation.

Both address analogy claim C89 comparing the mechanism to microtubule gliding assays. OpenEval finds the comparison mechanistically sound. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall mechanistic model without objection.

OpenEval evaluates claims C68-C70 regarding control experiments with varying antibody concentrations and asymmetry in escape events. These methodological controls are found to support experimental rigor. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific control experiment claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1, C8-C21, C92-C93, C116 as well-established background facts from literature appropriately cited. These represent accepted knowledge providing context for experimental findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/literature claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C117-C122 describing experimental controls and analysis procedures, particularly the control showing minimal bead attachment without antibody crosslinking. These methodological details support experimental rigor. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological control claims.
